title: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition Hits 91 on Metacritic After Switch 2 Performance Fears
description: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition is now available on Nintendo Switch 2, and final reviews suggest FromSoftware has turned a worrying early port into a surprisingly strong handheld version of the Lands Between.
body:
Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition is heading into its Nintendo Switch 2 launch with a far stronger critical reception than its troubled road to release once suggested. The new edition is currently sitting at 91 on Metacritic based on 31 critic reviews reported in the latest review roundups, with reviewers repeatedly highlighting how well FromSoftware’s enormous open-world RPG has survived the move to Nintendo’s hybrid hardware.

That reception is particularly notable because Tarnished Edition spent much of its pre-release cycle under a cloud of performance concerns. Earlier demonstrations raised questions about whether the Switch 2 version could deliver the consistency Elden Ring demands. After additional development time, however, the final release is being described by several reviewers as a surprisingly accomplished port.

Tarnished Edition launches on August 28, 2026, and includes Elden Ring, the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, and additional content created for this release.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition key art for Nintendo Switch 2, featuring a Tarnished from FromSoftware’s acclaimed open-world action RPG.

contentBlocks.text: Ahead of launch, review roundups reported a **91 Metacritic score from 31 critic reviews**, a striking result for a port whose technical condition had become part of the story.\n\nNow that Tarnished Edition is actually available, full final-build reviews reinforce the broader point behind that early score: critics are largely finding that Elden Ring survives the move to Switch 2 far better than its troubled pre-release demonstrations suggested. The precise Metacritic average and review count can continue to move as additional reviews are added, so the more durable story is the strength of the overall reception rather than a permanently fixed number.
contentBlocks.heading: A 91 Metacritic score changed the conversation

contentBlocks.text:
The path to release was not straightforward. Earlier Switch 2 demonstrations raised serious performance concerns, making the quality of the finished port one of Tarnished Edition’s biggest questions.

Final reviews paint a considerably better picture. Nintendo Wire reports that the game targets **30 FPS in both handheld and docked modes** and says it maintained that target most of the time across more than 20 hours of play, although occasional slowdowns still occurred. UnGeek likewise describes the final build as very playable while noting drops below the 30 FPS target in demanding open-world situations. WorthPlaying calls the finished version generally consistent despite clear visual and frame-rate compromises.

The important distinction is that Tarnished Edition is not suddenly the technically definitive version of Elden Ring. The Switch 2 release still makes compromises, and different reviewers report different levels of slowdown. What has changed is that the final build is being reviewed as a viable, enjoyable port rather than the technical problem many feared.
contentBlocks.heading: From performance fears to a much stronger final port

contentBlocks.text: The Switch 2 version’s strongest argument is portability. Several reviews emphasize how impressive it is to have Elden Ring’s enormous world available as a handheld experience, even when the image and performance cannot match PlayStation 5, Xbox Series consoles or a capable PC.\n\nThat advantage also helps explain why assessments of docked and handheld play vary. Some reviewers report a remarkably consistent experience between the two modes, while others prefer handheld presentation because the smaller display makes visual compromises less noticeable. The consensus is therefore less “Switch 2 is the best version” and more “this is a surprisingly credible portable version of Elden Ring.”
contentBlocks.heading: Handheld play may be Tarnished Edition’s real advantage

contentBlocks.text: **Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition includes the base game and Shadow of the Erdtree expansion** on Switch 2, alongside the new Tarnished Pack content. Bandai Namco’s August 28 launch announcement confirms two additional starting classes — **Heavy Knight and Idus Knight** — four new armor sets and three appearance options for Torrent.\n\nPatch 1.17 adds further detail. The new starting-class equipment can also be obtained elsewhere in the Lands Between, additional weapons have been added, and the update introduces **two new NPC invasion events**, one in Caelid and another in Leyndell, Royal Capital. The Tarnished Pack content is included by default with Tarnished Edition and is also available separately for existing Elden Ring players on supported platforms.
contentBlocks.heading: Tarnished Edition includes more than the original game

contentBlocks.text:
Tarnished Edition launched on **August 28, 2026**, marking Elden Ring’s first appearance on a Nintendo platform. For players who prioritize maximum image quality or higher performance, the existing console and PC versions remain stronger choices.

But that is no longer the most interesting question surrounding this release. After the concern created by its early demonstrations, FromSoftware has delivered a Switch 2 version that reviewers broadly consider capable of preserving the scale, combat and atmosphere that made Elden Ring exceptional.

That makes Tarnished Edition less a story about whether Switch 2 can run Elden Ring at all and more about the compromises players are willing to accept in exchange for taking the Lands Between with them.
contentBlocks.heading: The turnaround is now the real story

conclusion: ==The strongest story surrounding Tarnished Edition may not be that Elden Ring remains an exceptional game four years later. It is that a Switch 2 version once defined by technical concern has reached launch with critics talking about how successfully FromSoftware turned it around. For players who have been waiting to explore the Lands Between on Nintendo hardware, August 28 now looks considerably more promising than the port’s early showings suggested.==
